product.summary: An open-source data platform that automates the ingestion, storage, retrieval, and transformation of petabyte-scale robot sensor data. Pitched as a Databricks for robotics, it handles multiple formats (ROS, ROS2, MCAP, etc.) through a single interface. Core feature: semantic search using natural-language queries to find physical sensor events (e.g., acceleration peaks, GPS drops, joint overloads).
product.problem_statement: Robotics engineers waste countless hours on data plumbing—manually searching files for sensor data needed to train or validate models, or building custom format converters. Existing databases cannot efficiently handle time-series multi-modal sensor data.
product.solution: Mosaico is a data layer that runs on-premises (on user infrastructure), consisting of an SDK (mosaico-sdk) and a daemon (mosaicod). It ingests and indexes sensor data, and returns timestamp windows for desired events across the entire dataset via SQL or natural-language queries. Data is transferred between SDK and daemon without conversion overhead.
key_features: Data Ontology: Automatically applies standard schemas for sensor data.
Multimodal Search: Search for physical events using natural-language queries.
Data Lineage: Tracks every transformation from raw sensor to training set.
Data Containers: Native support for ROS, ROS2, and MCAP formats with optimal compression.
Orchestrator: Automates labeling, segmentation, and inference pipelines.
Certifiability: Supports enterprise regulatory compliance.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Follows an open-core model (Apache 2.0)—adds enterprise features on top of an open-source core engine. Provides C++/Python SDKs. Adapts a Databricks-style data lakehouse approach to the robotics domain.
product.target_customer: Robotics companies and research labs dealing with petabyte-scale sensor data, such as autonomous driving, drones, logistics robots, and manufacturing robots. Initial community members include engineers from Google DeepMind, Amazon, Zoox, Hexagon, ETH Zürich, EPFL, and Politecnico di Milano.
product.business_model: Open-source community-driven growth strategy. Currently focused on expanding the community; plans to monetize through paid features such as enterprise licenses, audit dashboards, access control, user management, and custom database connectors. Proof-of-concept projects with large industrial customers are underway.

direct_competitors.comparison: Foxglove is strong in ROS data visualization and debugging, but Mosaico covers the entire lifecycle: data collection, storage, search, and transformation—and offers an open-source engine.

baud-cerelyze-inc-2026.tagline: A company building AI training and inference chips that replace multiplication with addition, eliminating the need for GPUs.
baud-cerelyze-inc-2026.team_highlights: Team of 4. Composed of experienced chip designers and deep learning engineers.

product.summary: An AI chip and developer platform that completely removes neural network multiplication operations and performs training and inference using only addition.
product.problem_statement: Existing GPUs/TPUs have multiplication circuits that take up most of the chip area and consume a lot of power, and memory bandwidth bottlenecks worsen as AI model sizes increase.
product.solution: Invented a new arithmetic representation that replaces multiplication with addition, integrating 10x more compute units and SRAM on the same die area. Verified on a 12nm GlobalFoundries process, targeting tape-out by end of this year.
key_features: No multiplication circuit needed (multiplier-free)
Weights compressed more than 10x with no loss in accuracy
Provides a compiler to convert PyTorch exportable models into own format
Already demonstrated on FPGA emulation cluster (50M parameter model, 125MHz on U200 FPGA, over 1,000 tokens/s)
Supports pre-training, SFT, RFT, and inference
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: A lossless neural network representation that replaces multiplication with addition. Removes multiplication in both forward and backward passes. Works with existing architectures (GLM, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek, Flux, Wan, etc.) without modification.
product.target_customer: Startups, research institutions, and companies that directly train new AI models.
product.business_model: Does not sell chips; instead provides prepaid capacity on FPGA emulation-based clusters to design partners. Plans to maintain the same model after future ASIC mass production.

direct_competitors.comparison: GPU tensor cores still use multipliers. Baud eliminates multiplication itself.
ASICs specialized for transformer operations, but still perform multiplication. Baud removes multiplication regardless of model architecture.
Wafer-scale engines use huge silicon area. Baud maximizes density with small cores.
Inference-only chip (Corsair). Baud also supports training.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Arithmetic representation that eliminates the multiplication operation itself. Claims 'order of magnitude' performance advantage with the same process and memory bandwidth.
competitive_landscape.moat: Patent-pending arithmetic representation and compiler. Until the first chip is mass-produced, software (compiler, distributed training stack) is the key barrier.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: No ASIC yet, so actual performance unverified. Promising in FPGA emulation, but gap with large competitors like NVIDIA is large. Differentiation is clear but market position is minimal.
